transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-08 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Recorded: yes
- Attendees: Samira Kline (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Head of ML, AstraComms), Raj Iyer (Infra), Priya Nambiar (Product), Owen (CTO, late)

Auto-summary: quick Console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage analytics, cost attribution, and pilot steps. Customer wants to understand how Redwood maps chat and embedding traffic to route-level spend, and whether dedicated or hosted is better for their compliance + latency needs. They requested security docs and a pilot SOW.

Topics covered: console overview, per-route dashboards, route tagging, cost breakdown, batching/kv cache impacts, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, VPC & KMS questions, pilot next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can wait another minute for owen but wanted to get started. i'm samira kline from redwood, ae on the account. miguel from engineering is on to run the demo.
[00:12] Jenna: hi, thanks, yep happy to be here. we've got about 45 mins, hopefully we can dig into cost stuff — that's the top ask from finance.
[00:18] Miguel: awesome. quick agenda: i will show the console, per-route dashboards, a couple of example cost breakdowns for chat vs embeddings, then q&a.
[00:25] Raj: quick note — we run most traffic through an internal gateway, so we care about per-route tags and attribution to teams. also, our compliance team will need audit logs and key management notes.
[00:33] Miguel: totally. the console has route-level tags and you can map them to teams, products, or cost-centers. we'll show a CSV export too.
[00:42] [screen-share starts, short pause, minor audio artifact]
[01:05] Miguel: okay pulling up the usage hub — top-left you see 'Routes' list, we've got filters by model, region, and timeframe. for your profile, we usually recommend looking at 30d sliding windows to catch bursty behavior.
[01:26] Jenna: can you show an example where a single API path produces both chat and embedding calls? our front end sometimes multiplexes requests.
[01:34] Miguel: yeah. here i've got a sample route 'frontend-chat-v2' and under 'operations' it shows breakdown by generation type. notice embeddings calls are tagged separately at the request-level but if your frontend multiplexes, we can add sub-route labels using a header you control. (note: there's an api for 'x-rd-route' header).
[01:53] Raj: so if we put that header in our gateway, billing maps per sub-route?
[01:58] Miguel: exactly. the console will attribute tokens and calls to that sub-route and you can see token-level cost. small caveat — for streaming responses we attribute tokens after they are emitted so you may see slight lag.
[02:12] Priya: is there an auto-suggest to group routes by team so my finance person doesn't need to manually tag?
[02:18] Miguel: yes, we have a tagging rule engine. you can auto-map based on path regex, header, or JWT claim. we'll show the rule UI in a sec.
[02:30] [15s pause while Miguel navigates UI; keyboard clicks audible]
[02:48] Miguel: here is the 'Per-route cost decomposition' view — top panel is total spend, then down is a stacked bar by model and by quantization level. you can also toggle to per-token cost and per-call cost.
[03:07] Jenna: what's 'quantization level' doing in a hosted environment? i thought that was only for on-prem.
[03:13] Miguel: good question. in redwood hosted we offer model variants that are quantized for cost savings — they're validated by our onboarding team. the console shows which routes used which variant, so you can see quality vs unit-cost tradeoffs. sometimes the model falls back to a higher-precision variant; the console records fallback events.
[03:30] Raj: fallback events — are those logged with request IDs and timestamps for auditing?
[03:35] Miguel: yes we capture event logs with rids, but for private deployment your team can ship logs into your log collector. in hosted we provide export and a retention window; we will include the SOC2 docs in follow-up.
[03:48] [crosstalk]
[04:00] Miguel: next i want to show how batching and prefix caching change the per-token cost estimates. on the right is a simulation panel where you can edit batch size and cache hit rate.
[04:12] Priya: do you have defaults for different workloads?
[04:15] Miguel: we ship presets — chat interactive (low-latency) uses smaller batches and favors cache for recurrent prefixes; high-throughput re-ranker uses larger batches. for your 512-token average chat with 60% repeat prefixes, we estimate a 22% cost reduction with the default cache policy. i'll run an example in a sec.
[04:37] [brief pause while Miguel adjusts simulation; mild background typing]
[04:48] Miguel: okay simulation run: baseline hosted gpt-like model at your token size, no quant, cost per 1000 tokens $X (placeholder), with caching we show effective per-1000 drop by ~18-24% depending on hit rate.
[05:02] Jenna: finance insists on an expected unit cost range. can you give a concrete CSV export we can plug into our cost model?
[05:09] Miguel: yes the 'Export' button will give you per-route token counts, model variants, cache-hit rates, and estimated spend for the period. i'll attach a sample CSV to the follow-up.
[05:18] [00:05 glitch — 'k' sound]
[05:27] Raj: switching gears — dedicated vs hosted. our compliance team prefers dedicated because of network separation, but it costs more. what's the threshold where dedicated makes sense?
[05:37] Samira: from a commercial standpoint, dedicated starts to be cost-effective once steady-state QPS and throughput exceed X tokens per month — we typically propose a committed pool. but also dedicated gives consistent tail latency SLAs and private network egress options.
[05:51] Miguel: technically, dedicated reduces noisy-neighbor variance and you can pin quantized kernels tuned for your model to get better unit costs at scale. hosted is easier for quick pilots.
[06:06] Raj: for VPC peering, does redwood support egress through our private subnet?
[06:11] Miguel: yes, for Redwood Private we do VPC peering and on-prem packages. for hosted we support an IP allowlist and TLS with customer-managed keys via KMS integration — we will share the network diagram.
[06:23] Jenna: okay, security checklist: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS. can you confirm all?
[06:31] Miguel: yes SOC2 report, SSO with SAML and SCIM for provisioning, role-based access via Console, request-level audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations for key material. i'll attach the documents.
[06:44] [phone joins, owen says hi]
[06:52] Owen: apologies for the delay — can you show how we can track cost per-feature? we want to charge product teams for different AI features.
[06:59] Miguel: absolutely. the 'Routes to Features' mapping shows cost per route and you can tag routes with feature ids. then the cost attribution workspace provides chargeback reports by tag across any date range. we also support mapping to your cloud billing center (if you want to pass through internal showback).
[07:18] Priya: is there a way to detect regressions in quality as we switch quantized variants? we need to make sure user-facing chat doesn't degrade.
[07:25] Miguel: yes, Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets — you can upload evaluation prompts and watch automatic quality alerts if responses diverge beyond a threshold after a rollout. you can also pin routes to a control variant during a canary.
[07:40] Jenna: we'd probably want a canary with 5% traffic before rolling.
[07:44] Miguel: perfect — the console supports that via rollout policies; you can do linear increases or custom triggers based on latency/error/quality metrics.
[07:53] [screen flicker, minor transcription glitch: 'kv cash' appears as k-v cash]
[08:05] Miguel: quick demo of a real per-route dashboard: here's 'billing-qa-route' — top shows total calls, median latency, p95, token consumption by direction, and a breakdown of token spend by model variant. see the small red dot? that's a fallback event on 2026-08-30 when the quantized variant exceeded memory and we fell back to full precision.
[08:28] Raj: can you export the fallback logs with the request ids so we can debug?
[08:32] Miguel: yes, export includes request IDs, timestamp, route, and reason code. for private deployments that export can flow to your SIEM.
[08:42] Jenna: hypothetical: if we need EU data residency, does Redwood hosted have region controls?
[08:48] Miguel: yes hosted supports region locking for data residency in EU regions. for strict residency and custom retention policies, Private is recommended.
[08:57] Priya: what about model updates? we cannot have changes that alter behavior in production without approval.
[09:03] Miguel: you can pin model versions per route. model catalog shows version hashes; changes need to be accepted in the console. we also support scheduled maintenance windows and automatic fallback to last-approved version.
[09:15] [short pause]
[09:22] Miguel: let's run a sample 'what-if' — i will load your traffic profile (sample we prepared from a similar customer) and show cost-per-feature.
[09:30] [typing]
[09:46] Miguel: loaded. here's per-feature spend: chat feature A — 62% of spend, embeddings for search — 28%, misc rerankers — 10%. by switching embeddings to quantized variant B we drop embeddings spend by ~40% with a small latency uptick.
[10:03] Jenna: that 40% is attractive. what's the expected impact on p95 latency?
[10:08] Miguel: about 10-30ms increase p95 for embeddings depending on region; we have region-specific benchmarks in the model catalog.
[10:16] Raj: any hidden egress or networking fees if we do Private?
[10:20] Samira: we include standard egress pricing in the dedicated quote; if you run on-prem there are different line items for support. we'll detail those in the SOW.
[10:31] Priya: okay can you show the exact CSV fields we would get? our finance wants to join to our chargeback pipeline.
[10:36] Miguel: sure — columns: route_id, route_name, feature_tag, date, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit_ratio, estimated_token_cost, total_route_cost, fallback_count, avg_latency_ms. i'll paste a sample after.
[10:49] Jenna: perfect.
[10:51] [10s pause while screen-share switches to export view]
[11:05] Miguel: also note the console can integrate with your billing system via webhook so each daily export can be pushed to your S3 or into a partner billing connector.
[11:15] Raj: is there an SLA for exports? we rely on daily reconciliation.
[11:19] Samira: exports are generated nightly for hosted, guaranteed within 24 hours; dedicated can do hourly exports as part of the committed package.
[11:28] Jenna: timeline — we want a pilot in the next 3 weeks, with results in 30 days to decide on a commit. is that realistic?
[11:36] Samira: Yes. pilot outline: 30-day pilot, limited to 3 routes, dedicated telemetry + console access, sample synthetic load test. we will provide a pilot SOW and pricing matrix.
[11:46] Priya: what about security review — can we start that in parallel?
[11:49] Miguel: absolutely. i'll send the SOC2 and network doc today and schedule a security deep-dive next week if you'd like.
[11:58] Owen: one more — are there limits on schema for route tags? we have long internal ids.
[12:02] Miguel: tags are freeform up to 128 chars. we recommend hierarchical tags like team:product:feature.
[12:09] Jenna: any competitor-related notes we should watch for — some groups asked about Anthropic's guardrails.
[12:15] Samira: we map policies and prompt safety differently; Redwood focuses on operational predictability and cost levers rather than model-level guardrails. if you need model safety layer, we can integrate third-party processors or your in-line filters.
[12:30] Raj: final question — do you provide rate-limiting per route?
[12:34] Miguel: yes per-route throttles, burst quotas, and dynamic autoscale policies for Dedicated. in hosted we have quotas per API key and token-based rate limits.
[12:44] [wrap-up]
[12:50] Samira: quick recap: we'll send pilot SOW + pricing, SOC2 & network/KMS docs, sample CSV and a perf estimate for your 512-token chat, and schedule a security deep-dive. next step is Raj and Samira to confirm kickoff date.
[13:06] Jenna: thanks, appreciate it. looking forward to the CSV and the SOW.
[13:10] Owen: thanks everyone.
[13:12] Miguel: i'll follow up with the export and perf numbers.
[13:18] [meeting ends, 52m recorded total — transcript truncated at end-of-call silence]
